claims.text: Operability/data, rollback path. A review left pending in a --checkpoint-db by this code, whose state now carries `ruleset`, resumes and finishes under the pre-change commit fd7b64c, which stands in for reinstalling the previous wheel. The memo is approved, and the evidence is grounded without the ruleset key. The test was added in this seat: tests/test_p7_history.py::test_rollback_a_review_left_pending_here_resumes_under_the_pre_change_version, marked contracts and dual_run. The forward direction, a pre-change pending review resumed here, is covered by test_a_review_left_pending_by_the_pre_change_version_resumes_here.

Security/input validation at the new entry point, CMA_RULESET. Only ids in the RULESETS allow-list load, so an id cannot name a path. The table is loaded with a SafeLoader subclass that refuses duplicate keys. Every field is type-checked, and patterns that do not compile (re.error, OverflowError, RecursionError) are refused. A damaged or missing table gives a refusal with exit 2 and is never reported as a model failure (exit 4). No new dependency: pyyaml>=6 was already in pyproject.toml:12. No secrets are added. The evidence gains only the ruleset id and hash, so it adds no personal data.
Static checks pass on the changed code, and the offline evals stay fully grounded under the default v1.
